name: Redensity

lead: Redensity is the name Teoxane uses for several hyaluronic acid products. RHA Redensity is a 'resilient' filler for dynamic areas such as the lines around the mouth, and Teosyal PureSense Redensity 2 is used in the tear trough under the eyes to soften hollows.

The gel adds support and hydration where it is placed, so creases look smoother and the under-eye area looks less hollow. A randomised, evaluator-blinded multicenter study of RHA Redensity for moderate-to-severe perioral lines ran 52 weeks against a no-treatment control, and a prospective observational study looked at Redensity 2 around the eyes.

paras: A clinician injects the gel under or into the skin of the target area, often the perioral lines or tear trough, and the smoothing is visible right away. The RHA range is described as stretching and returning with facial movement, and treatments are repeated as the gel gradually breaks down.

Typical effects of hyaluronic acid fillers include swelling, bruising and lumps, with vascular and delayed inflammatory reactions rarer. Hyaluronic acid filler can be dissolved with hyaluronidase, and a 2023 study tested how 21 fillers respond to it.

chain: HA gel fills lines and hollows
angle.text: Teoxane's Redensity hyaluronic acid gels smooth lines around the mouth and soften under-eye hollows, with the change visible as soon as the gel is placed. A randomised 52-week trial studied RHA Redensity for perioral lines.

lead: Redensity refers to hyaluronic acid (HA) products from Teoxane, including RHA Redensity (a 'resilient' HA filler) and Teosyal PureSense Redensity 1 and 2.[1][2][3]

A randomised, evaluator-blinded multicenter study of RHA Redensity for moderate-to-severe dynamic perioral rhytides ran for 52 weeks against no-treatment control, with the aim of demonstrating superiority.[1] A prospective observational study of Redensity 2 in the periorbital region examined real-world efficacy and safety.[3]
Other work covers laboratory studies of non-crosslinked Redensity 1 as a cell carrier in burn management,[4] cannula delivery for skin density,[5] and responsiveness to hyaluronidase.[2]

paras: The 52-week randomised perioral study with blinded evaluators compared RHA Redensity with no treatment.[1] A prospective observational study of Teosyal PureSense Redensity 2 in real-world practice assessed under-eye (tear trough) treatment.[3] A retrospective controlled ultrasound study examined cannula-assisted delivery of an HA-based hydrogel for facial skin density.[5]

Registered trials include perioral rhytids,[6] infra-orbital hollows versus no treatment,[7] crow's feet with a micro-needle device,[8] radial cheek lines,[9] and anaesthetic-containing versions.[10][11]
In a 2023 in-vitro study, 21 HA fillers were each exposed to recombinant human hyaluronidase, comparing how readily they dissolved.[2] Clinical safety is reported within the trials above.
